name: Tung Chee Chen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Chee Chen was the chairman and chief executive of Hong Kong-listed Orient Overseas, one of Hong Kong's last great shipping dynasties.
In 2018 Tung Chee Chen and his brother, Tung Chee Hwa, sold their entire 68.7% stake to China shipping giant COSCO.
The sale netted the brothers $4.3 billion.
Founded in 1947 by his father, Tung Chao Yung, the empire has offices in more than 100 countries.

name: Mark Leonard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Mark Leonard founded Canadian tech company Constellation Software in 1995.
Constellation Software, also known as CSI, acquires, manages and builds software businesses.
Leonard and members of his family own an estimated 7% of the company, which is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
He was Constellation's president until stepping down in October 2025. He remains on the board.
After getting an MBA from the University of Western Ontario, Leonard worked in venture capital for 11 years.
forbes_facts: There are few known photos of the elusive billionaire, who has never talked to the press.
According to Canada's Globe and Mail, Leonard worked "as a banker, valuator, mason, gravedigger, dog handler, bouncer, sapper, and wind energy researcher."

name: Xue Min
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Xue Min controls Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare, a supplier of medical equipment for imaging and radiation therapy.
The company sells to 50 countries, including the U.S., Italy, Japan and New Zealand.
It went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's Sci-Tech Innovation Board in 2022.
Earlier, in 1998, Xue founded Shenzhen Mindit Instruments, which was later acquired by  Siemens Medical Solutions.

name: Mark Davis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Mark Davis owns the Las Vegas Raiders, the NFL team he inherited from his father, Al Davis (d. 2011).
Davis' only jobs have ever been with the team. He worked first in the equipment room, then in team retail, where he is said to have invented the muff-style hand warmer that is now used league-wide.
Davis moved the Raiders from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020 after a failed attempt to relocate to Los Angeles.
When Davis took over, Forbes valued the team at $761 million. Now, it's worth more than $7 billion.
He also owns the Las Vegas Aces WNBA team.

name: Adam Kwok
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Adam Kwok's father, Thomas, is the second-oldest son of the late Kwok Tak-seng, cofounder of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
Thomas was the company's cochairman from 2011 until 2014, when he was sentenced to five years in prison for bribing a government official.
In Thomas's absence, Adam has served as an executive director at the company.
forbes_facts: Four of Adam's cousins are also billionaires, along with his father, an uncle and grandmother.

name: Wang Jian
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2018-2022); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2022)
forbes_bio: Wang Jian is the president of BGI, one of Asia's largest genomics companies.
Wang worked as a senior research fellow at the University of Washington between 1990 and 1994.
Wang Jian graduated from Central South University and holds a master's degree from Beijing University of Chinese Medicine.
After graduation, he performed postdoctoral research at the University of Texas and the University of Iowa from 1988 to 1990.

name: Kalanithi Maran
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Politician's son Kalanithi Maran dabbled in his family's modest publishing business before launching Sun TV Network in 1993.
Sun is now a regional television heavyweight with 37 channels reaching more than 140 million households in India.
In June 2024 it launched a Hindi entertainment channel called Sun Neo.
Maran's other interests include newspapers, radio and direct-to-home television.
His wife, Kavery, is an executive director at Sun TV Network and oversees content.
forbes_facts: Maran and his brother Dayanidhi, a former telecom minister, were embroiled in a telecom corruption case but were cleared of all charges.
Sun owns Sunrisers Hyderabad, an Indian Premier League cricket team.
In August 2025 Sun TV Network said that the legal notice served in June by his younger brother Dayanidhi, alleging share transfer disputes in 2003, was withdrawn.

name: Chetan Dube
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2022)
forbes_bio: Chetan Dube is the founder of New York City-based artificial intelligence company Amelia, whose flagship product is an eponymous chatbot.
Amelia's conversational AI technology provides customer service for about 500 corporate clients, including Telefonica, BNP Paribas and Nordic Bank.
Indian-born Dube moved to the United States after college to become an applied mathematics professor at New York University in 1992.
He left academia and started Amelia as information technology firm IPSoft in 1998, growing it to about $100 million in revenue in 2020.

name: Sergei Studennikov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Sergei Studennikov is founder of the Krasnoye & Beloye (Red & White) chain of self-service liquor stores, the largest liquor retailer in Russia.
In 2019, he merged it with the Dixy supermarket chain owned by billionaires Igor Kesaev and Sergei Katsiev to form Mercury Retail Group Limited.
Mercury Retail, in which he and his wife have a 49% stake, is the leading alcohol retailer in Russia with 15,000 stores.
Mercury postponed its much anticipated IPO after Putin invaded Ukraine.
In the 1990s, Studennikov founded a company that distributed vodka, beer and tobacco. He opened his first Red & White store in Kopeysk in 2006.

name: Larry Connor
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Larry Connor is a real estate investor in Dayton, Ohio who founded and leads the Connor Group, which invests in luxury apartment buildings across the U.S.
The Connor Group currently owns and operates a $5 billion portfolio of 51 apartment buildings across 12 states from Colorado to Florida. The firm keeps properties for 5 and a half years on average.
Connor founded the firm in 1991 with two partners, which he later bought out in 2003. The firm's annual rate of return is 30.4% and it has sold more than $6 billion worth of properties since 1995.
He traveled to the Mariana Trench, the deepest point on Earth, on a research voyage in 2021 and took part in Axiom Space's Ax-1 mission to the International Space Station in 2022.
In 2024 he opened the Greater Dayton School, Ohio's first private non-religious elementary school dedicated to under-resourced students.
forbes_facts: In September 2023, he broke the world record for the highest HALO formation skydive at 38,139 feet alongside a team of four U.S. Air Force pararescue specialists.
His first jobs included painting houses, selling "damaged label" wines to college students and picking up dead bodies for $5 apiece to bring to a local funeral home.

name: Taylor Swift
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Taylor Swift became a billionaire in October 2023, thanks to the earnings from her Eras Tour and the value of her music catalog.
Swift is the first musician to make the billionaire ranking primarily based on her songs and performances.
Her fortune includes nearly $800 million amassed from royalties and touring, plus a music catalog worth an estimated $600 million and some $110 million in real estate.
In May 2025, Swift announced that she had finally re-acquired the rights to her first six albums, which she'd been re-recording and releasing since 2021.
Demand for tickets to the U.S. leg of her Eras Tour overwhelmed Ticketmaster, prompting members of Congress to question the company's hold on concert sales.
forbes_facts: After releasing her album "Midnights" in 2022, Swift became the first artist in history to claim the top ten spots on the Billboard Hot 100 song list.
